pull_requests.title: Cover guard: tests that only share an identifier with the diff do not demote a missing_test
pull_requests.body:
After #249, test-candidates.txt also lists tests that only share an identifier or literal with the diff (reason `mentions changed X`). post.js passed all of a file's candidates to the cover guard, so an unrelated test containing the claim's literal could demote a real missing_test (the #217 logger-test case).

Fix: `parseCandidates(text, { skipHunk: true })` drops hunk-tier entries; only the cover-guard call in src/post.js uses it. Other callers (focus ranking, pack-cut checks) and the model's context still see them. Side effect: a file whose only candidates are hunk-tier now has an empty guard scope, so no literal demotion (same as no candidate test).

Test: post.test.js 'the real cover guard: a hunk-tier candidate test that shares the literal does not demote...' (fails on main: finding is demoted; control with a same-stem candidate still demotes).

pull_requests.title: Test candidates: rank tests that use the identifiers the diff changes, and stop generic stems filling the cap
pull_requests.body:
## What

Test candidates (`test-candidates.txt`) now rank tests that use the identifiers the diff changes, and a generic stem can no longer fill the 5-slot cap.

- New tier in `mapTests` (src/test-map.js), after same-name / file-name / calls and before `mentions`: tokens (camelCase, snake_case, numbers of 5+ digits) from each changed file's added and removed lines (`git diff -U0`) are searched in the tests with one batched `git grep -o -w -F` per run. Tokens used by more than 25 test files are dropped. Score is idf x (1 + log count) per token, +100 when the test's stem is the token. Top 3 per file, reason "mentions changed `bodyLimit`".
- Bounds: 40 tokens per file, 200 per PR, 20 s per git call. A cut or a failed search is appended to `collect-limits.txt`.
- `mentions` tier: a stem named by more than 25 tests is skipped when the list is capped. The audit scan (per = Infinity) is unchanged.
- The cap stays 5.

## Evidence (eval/trace-recall, fastify, 12 cases x C/RC, code->req tests)

| | Hit@1 | Hit@3 | Recall@3 | MRR | All-required@3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4/24 | 4/24 (17%) | 4/54 (7%) | 0.167 | 2/24 |
| this PR | 18/24 | 20/24 (83%) | 28/54 (52%) | 0.813 | 6/24 |

req->code (code, file level, tests) and code->req requirement are identical to main. `baseline.json` has an `after_hunk_tokens` entry.

Overfitting check. Most of the gain is one file (test/internals/initial-config.test.js). With it removed from the ground truth: Hit@3 4/24 -> 14/24 (58%), Recall@3 4/42 -> 16/42, MRR 0.167 -> 0.424, Hit@1 4/24 -> 6/24. Still a clear gain, but the headline 83% overstates it.

SpecGuard's own last 10 merged PRs (merge^1..merge, no model): mean candidates per changed file 4.05 -> 4.29. A changed test file of the PR itself is in the top 3 for 16/18 files before and 17/18 after (PRs that changed tests only). It did not drop.

## Tests (src/collect.test.js)

- a test that uses the changed identifier is a candidate though it never names the file (fails on main)
- an identifier used by more than 25 tests produces no candidates (control, passes on main)
- 30 tests naming the stem do not fill the cap; the changed-symbol test is in the top 3 (fails on main)
- a huge hunk hits the 40-token cap and records a collect limit (fails on main)
- same-name test still ranks first, no limit recorded when no bound is hit (fails on main only for the added hunk candidate; the same-name order is unchanged)

Existing collect.test.js tests are unchanged. test-map.test.js and audit-units.test.js pass.

## Not done / notes

- Text match only: a test that shares a literal with the diff can rank. Three slots at most, after the name tiers.
- Repos with very many tests and a huge diff are bounded by the token caps and 20 s timeout; the cut is shown in collect-limits.

pull_requests.title: Weekly report: blind-label summary-only findings on the same IDs as fix-through, and stop presenting P×A as a measured rate
pull_requests.body:
Fixes review 2026-10-17 M5 (section 5.4) and the P x A finding (section 5.5).

**M5.** #233 put summary-only findings into fix-through (counts `sum`, synthetic priors), but `findingsOf` read only inline review comments. One summary-only finding added findings=1 and A=1 to fix-through and 0 blind-label candidates.
- `findingsOf` now also yields each finding in the latest sticky summary's counts `sum`, with `delivery: 'summary'` (inline ones get `delivery: 'inline'`). Its ref is the 16-hex fp prefix #233 tracks, so labels and per-finding outcomes join on one id. A finding present inline and in `sum` (same PR, fp prefix) counts once, as inline.
- Blind labels, findings per PR, overlap and unique all use the one list. `label-export` exports summary-only findings with a new `delivery` column (summary rows link to the sticky comment; the counts hold no finding text, only kind/path/line).
- The report adds a per-channel table (inline, summary, combined): pool size, fix-through findings and A, precision, unique/valid. Raw counts are shown. Existing thresholds are untouched.
- Counts written before #233 carry no `sum`, so they add nothing; the report says summary-only findings are tracked from 2026-10-17.

**P x A.** The F2 line is kept but now reads "P × A (economic assumption, not a measured joint rate)". A new section reports the measured joint: valid AND addressed over labelled findings that have an observed outcome (not_observed excluded), with counts. Below the 30-label target it prints "insufficient data"; if no labelled id has an outcome it says the joint was not computed.

**Invariant restored.** Precision and fix-through are computed over the same exposure set, joined by the same finding id; P x A is no longer presented as a measured rate.

**Tests** (weekly-report.test.js, label-export.test.js). Seven fail on main (main's two source files swapped in): the label-export `delivery` column test, "M5: a summary-only finding is a blind-label candidate...", "M5: the same fp inline and in sum counts once...", and four "P x A" tests (joint computed, insufficient data, mismatched ids, F2 label). Controls that pass on main: "M5 control: ...outside the usable set", "control: the existing report lines are unchanged", and the existing CLI fixture test. Touched test files: 29/29 pass.

**Not fixed.**
- The `outcomes` list in counts drops its oldest entries when long, so channel outcome counts can be below the combined `since` tally (stated in the report).
- The `delivery` column unblinds SpecGuard rows (only SpecGuard has summary-only findings); the plan says to judge on the text.
- Finding text for summary-only findings is not exported (counts do not store it).

**User-visible change.** The weekly report has a channel table and a P x A section; the label CSV has a `delivery` column; docs/validation-plan.md gains a note under the metrics table.

pull_requests.title: Eval: versioned requirement↔code retrieval set (fastify, 12 cases × R/C/RC) with Recall@K, MRR and All-required; parse thousands separators in size values

## What

1. `eval/trace-recall/`: the fastify traceability harness that measured #239, now in the repo and pinned to fastify `37df44a4`.

   - `run.js`: one cross-platform Node script. Fetches the pinned commit, makes R/C/RC local commits, runs `src/trace.js` and the `candidates()` script taken from `src/collect.sh` itself. No model. Writes `results.json` (git-ignored).

2. `sizeVariants`: `1,048,576`, `1_048_576` and thin/narrow-space grouping are read as one number, only as exact 3-digit groups.

| Recall@3 | 15/58 items | 26/58 items |
| MRR@10 | 0.444 | 0.750 |

A fresh `run.js` on this branch reproduces the after-#239 row rank for rank (58 of 58 locations equal to the earlier harness). code->req: requirement Hit@3 15/24 in both rows, test candidates Hit@3 4/24.

pull_requests.title: Status says whether the review finished; the fast-tier grade is reported separately
pull_requests.body:
## What changes
`specguard:status`, the `status` output and fail-on-error now say only whether execution finished. A fast-tier model alone no longer makes a run `incomplete`. The grade stays in `counts.tier` / `counts.reduced` and shows as a one-line note: "Fast-tier model: only high-confidence findings are posted inline."

Headline for a fast-tier run: gaps found -> ❌ (as before); unknowns / needs a person -> ❔ (as before); no findings and nothing cut -> "✅ Review complete (fast model): no high-confidence gaps". ⚠️ Incomplete only when the run is genuinely incomplete (cut context, timeout, collection or delivery gaps, the existing `incomplete` causes).

## Unchanged on purpose
- Counts fields `complete` (= execComplete && !reduced), `execution_complete`, `reduced`, `tier` keep meaning and values.
- Stale-thread auto-resolve still requires `complete` (full strength). Control test added.
- `outcome_valid` / fix-through attribution untouched.
- Reduced-mode behaviour (inline cap 3, two citations, high confidence) untouched.

## Head marker
Confirmed from the code: `headSha` was passed to buildSummary only when `!incomplete.length && !reduced`. Now it is `!incomplete.length && !struggling`, so a fast-tier but execution-complete run writes `specguard:head`, and a re-run on the same head is skipped by preflight (reuses the verdict).

## Consumers of status / head marker
| Consumer | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| post.js state / `status` output (L1465) | fast tier -> `incomplete` | fast tier alone -> `complete` |
| post.js head marker (buildSummary `headSha`) | not written for reduced | written for fast-tier-only; still not written for the other reduced triggers or `incomplete` |
| post.js `keepPrior` (failed re-run keeps prior summary) | prior status must be complete/incomplete (reads status marker) | same; a fast-tier prior is now `complete`, still accepted |
| preflight.js `sticky` | skips only when head marker present; fast-tier runs always re-reviewed | fast-tier-only runs are skipped on same head/req/cfg |
| fail-on-error.js | `incomplete` + counts.reduced -> warning "ran a reduced review" | `complete` + counts.reduced -> `::notice::` fast-tier review; `incomplete` + reduced (struggling run) keeps the reduced warning; exit codes unchanged |
| eval/grade.js (L75-77) | uses `execution_complete` counts first, status marker only as fallback for old summaries | unchanged behaviour; fallback now also reads fast-tier as complete (correct) |
| eval/aggregate-counts.js | reads `outcome_valid` / `complete` counts | unchanged (counts unchanged) |
| eval/weekly-report.js | counts `complete` | unchanged |
| action.yml `status` output / fail-on-error env | passes post.js status | fast-tier runs now report `complete` |

## Scan mode (audit-post.js)
Checked: audit-post.js has no reduced/tier logic; scan status is `incomplete` only for real coverage gaps (partial, blocks not audited, unit call failed, reached-not, etc.). Nothing to change.

## Other reducedReasons triggers
Decision: keep today's behaviour (reduced AND incomplete) for all three; only the fast-tier trigger changed.
- Repair finalized / repair turn needed or failed: the engine ran out of budget or its output was malformed; the answer is partial or repaired. Execution gap -> incomplete.
- >=3 engine notes: engine reported problems during the run. Execution gap -> incomplete.
- >25% obligations degraded by validation: the model's own citations failed on a quarter of the rows; coverage is genuinely missing. Execution gap -> incomplete.
Implementation: `gradeOnly(reduced)` is true only when the sole reason is `fast-tier model`. A fast tier plus any other trigger stays incomplete.

## Tests
New / changed (all fail on main; verified by swapping in main's post.js and fail-on-error.js: 5 failures):
- `reduced: a fast-tier run with no findings is "Review complete (fast model)" and complete; ...` : status complete, ✅ headline, head marker, counts reduced true / complete false / execution_complete true; repair trigger control stays incomplete with no head marker.
- `status separates finishing from grade: ...` (new): fast tier with gaps -> ❌ + complete + output `complete`; stale thread NOT resolved (control); fast tier with context cut -> ⚠️ incomplete, no head marker, output `incomplete`.
- `fail-on-error.js ...` (updated): `complete` + reduced exits 0, prints notice, no incomplete warning; full-strength complete prints nothing (control); incomplete + reduced wording kept.
- Updated, each because it asserted "fast tier => incomplete / no head marker / old wording": `reduced: fast tier posts at most 3 inline ...` (status complete, head marker present, new note wording); `layout: the full visible order ...` (the note text is now "> Fast-tier model"). The `layout: incomplete, reduced and failed...` test is untouched (it uses a two-reason reduced run, still the old behaviour).

Local: post.test.js + audit-action.test.js 313 pass, 0 fail. Full suite is the CI gate.

## Behaviour change users will notice
Fast-tier PRs no longer show the incomplete status or the retry on every push of the same head; the summary gets a one-line fast-tier note instead. A fast-tier run with an empty result now reads ✅ "Review complete (fast model)" instead of "⚠️ Reduced review".

pull_requests.title: Scan test matching: import-path, dotted/kebab stems, plural fold and class-name tiers, ranked above word mentions
pull_requests.body:
The scan claimed "no test" for units whose spec exists (real nestjs/nest scan, clone at c215fd9). Fix is in `src/audit-units.js` only; `test-map.js` is untouched.

**Cause**
- A1 `multer.constants.ts`: its stem has a dot, so it never entered the mentions tier; `export const X = {` yields no public name, so the calls tier got 0.
- A3 `listener-metadata-explorer.ts` vs `listeners-metadata-explorer.spec.ts`: plural differs and the stem is kebab-case.
- A2 `messages.ts`: 19 of 20 slots went to specs containing the common word "messages".

**Change** (test matching in `inventory()`; `mapTests` is called uncapped and the result is re-ranked by `rankTests`)
1. Import tier: a test whose relative import/require resolves to the unit (extension optional, `index` folder import) is matched. Reuses the `importShas` parser (now `importPaths`).
2. Dotted/kebab stems match only as whole path-like tokens (`multer.constants`, `listener-metadata-explorer`), not as their parts.
3. Plural fold on the stem (`listener` / `listeners`, any segment), only when the folder relation holds (same folder, below it, or mirrored under a `test/` segment).
4. A unit class named like the PascalCase stem (`ListenerMetadataExplorer`) counts as a mention.
5. Order: exact stem > import > plural fold > file-name/calls > class or stem token > word mention > same folder. The cap of 20 is filled in that order, so common words only take the leftover slots.
6. `export const|let|var NAME` yields NAME (wrapper around `publicDefs`).

**Tests** (`src/audit-units.test.js`, "test matching: ..."): A1-shaped (+ unrelated `constants.spec.ts` in another package not matched, + `export const` name), dotted token vs its parts, A3-shaped (import > plural fold > class; plural name in an unrelated package not matched), A2-shaped (25 word-only specs + 1 importer: importer first, 20 kept), index-folder import and exact stem still first. All fail on origin/main's `audit-units.js`; the file passes with the change (39/39).

**Real nest clone, 1015 units** (before -> after): matched tests 1173 -> 3609, mean 1.16 -> 3.56, p95 5 -> 20, max 20 -> 20, units with no test 625 -> 306. The additions are mostly real importers; 44 tests were dropped from 10 units, mostly word-mention noise displaced by importers.

**Behaviour change**: more units now read as tested (fewer "no test" leads); a unit imported by many specs fills its 20 slots with importers. Not done: transitive imports, bare-package imports, other languages' imports.

pull_requests.title: Scan precision: demote missing/weak test claims that a repo-wide symbol hit, a sibling test or a baseline system already answers
pull_requests.body:
Fixes the false positives found by hand-labelling full-repo scans on nestjs/nest c215fd9 and microsoft/TypeScript 9de8b7a (counted precision 1/11). All changes sit in the scan verify path (`verifyUnits` in src/audit-post.js, `makeCoverGuard` in src/test-map.js) and use the existing low-confidence channel (`low` + `lowWhy`, Details only, not counted). src/audit-units.js and audit-collect.js are untouched.

**Changes**
1. Symbol-reference fallback. A `missing_test` that the existing cover guard did not demote: take `enclosingName` of the cited line (now also sees `public *gen(` and `export const X = {`). If it is >= 5 characters, not in a small stoplist, and appears as a whole word (case-sensitive `git grep -w`) in any tracked test file, repo-wide, under the run's test classification, the finding is low: "may be covered by <path:line>". At most 50 searches per result. A method that another non-test file also defines (Go `func (t *X) Name(`, a class method) is not searched: its name says nothing about this unit. A search that fails or times out is no hit.
2. Sibling refutation for `weak_test`. An identifier shared by the cited assertion and the counterexample is called in another test of the same file (same describe block, or +-40 lines) and that test asserts something: low, citing that line. "Asserts" is any assertion line, not only a value assertion: the real A4 sibling asserts `expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalled()`, which the weak-assertion tier calls weak.
3. Baseline test system. >= 200 tracked files under `testdata/baselines/`, `tests/baselines/` or `__snapshots__/` (detected from the tracked paths in audit-post): every scan `missing_test` is low with "this repository tests through baselines (<dir>, N files); check whether a baseline exercises it", plus one validation note.
4. Non-finding guard. A unit finding whose title or body matches `\bno (gap|finding)\b|\bcovered; no\b` is dropped, with a validation note.
5. Prompt rule in skills/spec-audit/SKILL.md (no `missing_test` for data-only tables, one-line accessors, build-tagged files; `weak_test` only if no other test in the describe asserts it). There is no .github mirror of spec-audit in this repo, so none was edited.

**Recall guard.** `tsc/internal/transformers/declarations/supplementalreferences.go:28` (labelled TP-valuable) is demoted ONLY by rule 3, the baseline rule. That is intended: baselines (e.g. compiler/contentMapperSupplementalModule.js) do exercise it. With the baseline rule disabled in the replay it stays counted; rules 1, 2 and 4 do not touch it (its method name `TransformSourceFile` is defined by every transformer, so rule 1 skips it).

**Replay of the real run-3 findings.json** (offline, clones at the scanned SHAs, matched tests from the inventory):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nest (8 findings) | 7 counted | 4 counted |
| TypeScript (6 findings) | 4 counted | 0 counted (baselines) |
| total counted | 11 | 4 |

Changed: multerExceptions (A1) low by rule 1; scanForClientHooks (A3) low by rule 1; utils.spec.ts:171 (A4) low by rule 2; the "covered; no finding" row dropped (rule 4; it was already low as no-sketch); the four TypeScript findings counted on main (enum, supplementalreferences, forawait, commonjsmodule) low by rule 3. Still counted: isDebugMode (one-line env getter, no symbol on the cited line to search; rule 5 prompt covers it), SHADOWED_ROUTE_MESSAGE, utils.spec.ts:197, isStaticPath. os_android.go and reparser.go were already low on main (delegated-helper hit).

**Tests** (all fail on main, shown by swapping in main's src files; controls pass on both)
- src/audit-code.test.js: `scan gate: a missing_test whose enclosing symbol ...` (A1/A3 shape plus controls: no hit stays, `run` too short/generic, plain covers has no symbol search), `... bounded to 50 findings`, `... a weak_test whose counterexample names a call ...` (A4 shape; control: no sibling call stays), `... >= 200 baseline files ... 199 files change nothing` (+ `__snapshots__`, weak_test unaffected), `... says there is no gap is dropped`.
- src/test-map.test.js: `enclosingName: a generator method and an exported constant table ...`, `symbol guard: ...` (real git repo: whole word only, unreferenced stays, method defined elsewhere is no hit).
- src/prompt.test.js: `audit prompt: no missing_test for data-only tables ...` (prompt pin).
- Changed existing test: in `summary: a gap on a higher_level row ...` the no-sketch finding was titled "... covered by unit tests; no gap found", which rule 4 now drops. Retitled it so the test still checks the no-sketch low path; the dropped case is covered by the new test.

Local runs: prompt, audit-code, test-map, audit-action, audit-units test files pass (158). Full suite is CI's.

**Not fixed / limits**
- Rule 1 is a name search, not a proof: a test that references a same-named symbol of another module can demote a real gap (it stays visible in Details).
- Trivial targets with no symbol on or above the cited line (e.g. isDebugMode) rely on the prompt rule only.
- Baseline repos: all scan `missing_test` become low, including real gaps.

User-visible: fewer counted unit gaps; low-confidence rows carry the reasons above.

pull_requests.title: Trace: search the requirement's heading and size forms, skip docs as code, and show the candidates the top-3 cut drops
pull_requests.body:
Measured on fastify 37df44a, `requirements_paths=docs/Reference/**`, doc-only changes, 12 cases x R/C/RC = 36 runs (harness: `trace-eval/`, real `trace.js`). Baseline: 26% recall@3, all required locations found in 1 of 12 cases.

## Changes (all in `src/trace.js`)
1. The requirement's heading goes into the code query. For "Default: `false`" the subject is the heading (`return503OnClosing`). `changedItems` carries `heading`; `requirementToCode` adds it to the query.
2. Documents (`docLike`) are never ranked as code.

Used for occurrence search and for the literals boosting code windows. `bytes` and `KiB/MiB/GiB` are now units in `values()`. A bare number counts only if it is a whole multiple of 1024.

5. The top-3 cut is visible. The top 3 are still shown; the next up to 5 paths go in `more` of the row, and a limitation says "N more code/test candidate(s) for <req> not shown (top 3 kept): paths". Principle 1.

pull_requests.title: scan_paths selects the units to review; requirements, tests and evidence are read from the whole repository
pull_requests.body:
## What
`scan_paths` now selects which units (source files) are reviewed. Requirement documents, matched tests and evidence are read from the whole repository (still subject to requirements_paths, ignore rules, test_paths and DENY).

## Why
Before, one predicate restricted everything the scan reads. Scoping a monorepo to `packages/core/**` hid a top-level `test/` and central `docs/`, so units got no test (false "no test" gaps) and central requirements were never read. Nothing in the report said so.

## Changes
- audit-collect.js: scope is no longer passed to doc discovery or the evidence search; the test layout hint gets the whole tree.
- audit-units.js: scope filters only the unit candidates; tests come from all non-skipped files.
- audit-post.js: the issue line is now "Units reviewed (scan_paths): ...; requirements, tests and evidence are read from the whole repository."
- action.yml and README: new meaning, and how to restrict documents (`requirements_paths` / `design_docs`).

## Tests
- New (audit-code.test.js): unit in `packages/core` matches top-level `test/`; `docs/design.md` is discovered under that scope; `packages/other` is not selected; control without scope is unchanged.
- Updated to the new contract: `audit-collect.test.js` "scan_paths: ..." (previously asserted docs/evidence were confined to the scope, which is the behaviour being changed on purpose), `audit-action.test.js` scan_paths description, two `audit-post.test.js` wording assertions.
- Both new/updated collect tests fail on main (assertions "the top-level test/ is matched", "the other package's documents are still read") and pass here. Also updated audit-units.test.js (scope no longer limits the tests an inventory unit matches). Full suite: CI.

## Budget
Discovery caps (2000 files, 500 docs), the evidence time budget and the inventory caps are unchanged; they now cover the whole tree, and hitting them still produces the same limitation notes. The README says so.

## Behaviour change
Scoped scans read more (all docs, all tests), so they can cost more and surface requirements from outside the package. Use `requirements_paths` to narrow documents.

## Scoped document blocks
Documents are discovered repo-wide, but a scoped run audits a block only when its document is in scope or at least one of its code candidates is. Other blocks are not sent or recorded; blocks with prior state are carried (as for the cap), and one limitation line lists them ("N document block(s) skipped: their evidence is outside scan_paths (...)"). Only applied when the evidence search completed; if it was cut or failed, nothing is skipped. The filter runs before the scan_max_blocks cap is applied: candidates are drawn in rounds, out-of-scope ones are set aside, and the cap is refilled from the next ranked blocks, so they never take slots from in-scope blocks (shared evidence time budget; if it ends, nothing more is skipped).

The dogfood "assertion removed" finding on audit-collect.test.js:315 is the intended contract inversion (docs and evidence are no longer confined to the scope).

comments.body: note: titles in the counts line take COUNTS_MAX space, and the trim loop drops `outcomes` first. So a PR with 20 summary findings keeps fewer per-finding outcomes, which is exactly the channel-split gap the new "trimmed" line reports. That's acceptable. But if the trimmed note starts appearing often in weekly reports, give `sum` titles their own small budget (for example 60 characters when outcomes are being dropped) rather than letting them crowd out outcomes. Also, two post tests double-counted finding text because the counts line repeats titles. Any future consumer that greps the comment body for finding text must strip the `specguard:counts` line first, and a one-line comment at `countsComment` would warn the next person.
